prompt:
The text below is drawn from , a measure of the priorities of the British electorate.



Below are two texts.

TEXT_C:
The Green Party’s 2005 manifesto sets out a realistic, values-driven programme for social, economic and environmental justice—putting people and planet before short-term profit, reversing privatisation, tackling inequality, and confronting climate change. It champions democracy, peace and localisation to build shared prosperity and long-term security.

- Economics: Tackle inequality with more progressive income tax bands, higher Corporation Tax for large firms, a progressive inheritance tax on recipients, and abolition of National Insurance in favour of broader income taxation. Pilot a Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates. Replace VAT with revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes that price resource use, waste and pollution. Back small firms, co‑ops and community banks; promote credit unions and local currencies; oppose UK entry to the euro; reform global trade rules. Create green jobs and defend workers’ rights; measure real progress beyond GDP.

- Energy and climate: Adopt Contraction and Convergence, cutting UK CO2 by 20% by 2010 on a path to 85% by 2030. Replace VAT/CCL on energy with a Carbon Tax, protecting low users. Reach 40% renewables by 2020 through major investment in wind, solar, wave and biogas, and shift R&D from nuclear to renewables. Cut demand via a Warmer Homes Act and Smart Energy Councils. Decommission nuclear as stations reach end of life.

- Welfare: Phase in a universal, non‑withdrawable Citizen’s Income to replace most means‑tested benefits; retain and then integrate housing benefit; keep disability/incapacity benefits additional. Establish a universal Citizen’s Pension linked to earnings, replacing Pension Credit. Support families by simplifying child support, raising Child Benefit, reducing working hours, and expanding Sure Start. Boost affordable housing through council building, self‑build co‑ops, LVT, and energy efficiency.

- Health and education: Restore the NHS to universal, comprehensive, publicly provided care; end PFI/PPP and foundation hospitals; oppose GATS in public services. Abolish prescription, eye test and dental charges; expand access to holistic care. Raise health spending to at least 9% of GNP, with a hypothecated NHS tax. In education, fund lifelong learning, expand pre‑school, scrap tuition fees and restore maintenance grants; abolish SATs and move toward Individual Learning Plans.

- Transport: Prioritise walking, cycling and public transport; cut road traffic 10% by 2010; re‑regulate buses; return rail and tube to public ownership; expand rail and light rail. Reflect true costs of motoring via congestion/road pricing, higher fuel duty and freight levies; invest in clean vehicle R&D. Resist airport expansion, ban night flights, and tax aviation fuel/emissions.

- Environment: Commit to Zero Waste with a ban on incineration, a national agency, and 60% recycling by 2010. Levy eco‑taxes on polluting inputs; create an Environmental Protection Commission. Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation and nanotech; oppose patents on genetic resources; strengthen animal welfare (end live exports, ban battery eggs, curb fur; replace vivisection).

- Food and farming: Pass an Organics Target Bill (30% by 2012); replace CAP/CFP with support for organic, local and biodiversity‑enhancing systems; ban GM food; curb supermarket market power.

- Crime and justice: Prevent crime by strengthening communities—better urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, treating drugs as a health issue; oppose ID cards. Expand accountable community policing. Enact strict gun controls. Embed restorative justice. Tackle hate crime, violence against women, and disability discrimination.

- Democracy: Renew local government with stronger powers, PR for councils and Westminster, referenda and recall; elected House of Lords; a written constitution, disestablishment of the Church, and curbed royal powers. Devolve regionally; enhance Scottish/Welsh powers. Oppose an undemocratic EU constitution while pursuing EU reform.

- Peace and international policy: Pursue an ethical foreign policy; oppose the Iraq war, replace UK troops with UN peacekeepers. Cut defence to the EU average; end arms export subsidies; back an Arms Trade Treaty; decommission nuclear weapons. Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI; cancel debts of the 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax. Reform the UN (end permanent Security Council seats) and democratise IMF/World Bank. Replace/transform WTO rules with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade favouring localisation, fairness and environmental limits. Uphold asylum rights: benefits, right to work, independent appeals; ratify migrant and refugee conventions.

TEXT_G:
UKIP’s 2005 manifesto argues that Britain’s real government now sits in Brussels and that no other reforms are possible until the UK leaves the EU. The party is not anti-European; it insists the best people to run Britain are the British. Its core aim is an independent, deregulated, free-trading Britain that restores democratic accountability, local control and traditional values of trust, responsibility and national pride.

Independence and timetable
- Repeal the European Communities Act to restore the supremacy of UK law, stop payments to the EU, regain an independent WTO seat and replace EU rules with UK-made laws in a two-year transition. Replace CAP and CFP with British policies and strike bilateral trade and cooperation deals with EU states.

Economy, regulation and trade
- Keep open trade with the EU via Swiss-style agreements; expand global trade with the Commonwealth, NAFTA and Asia; regain leverage at the WTO to press for freer trade.
- Scrap damaging EU-derived regulations, with a presumption to repeal unless retention is overwhelmingly justified, prioritising relief for small firms and ending rules like the Working Time Directive.

Budget and tax
- Redirect UK contributions to the EU to raise state pensions; temporarily raise borrowing (to about a 6% deficit) to fund immediate tax cuts and defence.
- Immediate tax changes: halve council tax for all, scrap the 10% income tax band, raise the inheritance tax threshold to £500,000, and reinstate dividend tax credits to rescue pensions.
- Longer term: simplify and cut taxes—merge National Insurance with income tax, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, and consider a low-rate flat tax to spur growth and reduce evasion.

Health, welfare and pensions
- End central micromanagement of the NHS; restore local control, bring back matrons, scrap SHAs, extend GP hours, and let clinicians treat on clinical need not targets. Allow complementary private insurance as in other countries.
- Simplify benefits, reduce means-testing and restore independence from welfare.
- Lift state pensions modestly using EU savings; reinstate dividend tax credits; unfreeze expatriate pensions. Reject mass immigration as a pensions fix.

Education
- Restore school autonomy; scrap SATs; back heads on exclusions; support discipline, sport, trips and teaching of British history and values. Encourage specialist schools with limited selection.
- Expand choice: assisted places, vouchers or tax rebates for private education.
- Review university standards, close weak courses, fully fund strong ones, cancel top-up fees, restore grants and charge EU students full fees.

Law and order, borders and asylum
- Tougher, credible sentencing; more local accountability of police; cut paperwork; defend homeowners; build prisons; resist EU Corpus Juris.
- Aim for near-zero net immigration: a non-discriminatory points system; end automatic EU preference; stricter family reunion; embarkation controls; language/“Britishness” tests; health checks; faster removals; redefine refugee rules. No quotas.

Farming and fishing
- Leave CAP; replace with deficiency payments/minimum prices; curb supermarket power; consider reviving the Milk Marketing Board; cut red tape; reopen local abattoirs; back green/organic methods.
- Leave CFP; reclaim UK waters; rebuild protection fleet; enforce conservation zones and gear rules.

Defence and foreign affairs
- Sovereign defence policy; maintain NATO ties; leave EU defence plans; reverse force cuts; buy British where possible; deploy only in the national interest; keep independent seats in global bodies.

Energy, environment and transport
- Stop wind farm rollout; build new nuclear; develop clean coal and fund fusion research.
- Take back control of environmental law; prioritise recycling; protect countryside; ban GM crop planting until proven safe.
- Invest in roads; set sensible speed limits and target cameras; choose rail structures that work (including reintegration if needed); continue upgrades.

Governance and civil liberties
- Defend the Commons, the Crown, common law and an independent Lords; citizen-initiated referendums at 5% of the electorate; English votes for English laws.
- Scrap English regional assemblies; return business rates and housing transfer duties to councils; cut politically correct bureaucracy.
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; reject the EU Charter; scrap ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.

Vision
An independent Britain—freer, safer, more prosperous—run by accountable institutions, with smaller government, stronger families, revitalised enterprise and a renewed sense of national purpose.

Judge whether TEXT_C or TEXT_G better reflects what these voters cared about.
